@graph.headline: The Revenge Trading Circuit-Breaker
@graph.description: How to stop revenge trading, step by step: fill in the circuit-breaker contract, repair a breach, and compare what honouring it costs versus chasing a loss.

mainEntity.name: What do I do after I break the breaker?

acceptedAnswer.text: Follow the 5-step breach repair in this workbook, in order: stop trading immediately, close breach positions, log the breach honestly, leave the desk and do your walk-away activity with no return today, and review tomorrow — not tonight — what to change in the contract. A breach does not cancel the contract; the repair is part of using it.

mainEntity.name: Does a scratch trade reset my consecutive-loss count?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, under this workbook's streak rule: a trade that ends flat or in profit — a scratch/breakeven trade or a win of any size — resets the consecutive-loss count to zero. Only a trade that loses money extends the count, so two losses separated by a scratch are not two consecutive losses.

mainEntity.name: How do I adapt the session stop for 24/7 crypto markets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Define a personal session window and a rolling loss limit in the crypto row of the contract: your window's clock times, and a loss limit measured over any rolling 24 hours rather than a calendar day. When either the 2-consecutive-loss stop or the rolling limit is hit, you stop until the window resets — the window replaces the market close that day traders get for free.

mainEntity.name: How do I pick a first number for my daily loss limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use the illustrative translation in this workbook, not a copied prescription: express a first fill-in value as a multiple of your normal risk per trade — for example, 3 times a 1% risk per trade gives a 3% first-fill figure to try — then adjust it from your own ledger. If hitting the number would leave you desperate to recover it the next morning, it is too large.

mainEntity.name: How does a swing trader adapt the cooldown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use the swing row of the contract: cooldown until the next session, instead of the 15–30 minute day-trading cooldown. The rest of the contract does not change — the session still stops at 2 consecutive losses or at the daily loss limit, whichever comes first, and returns are still at half size under the winner-test.
